items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1973-12-30
items.q: Charlie Dixon was one of the greatest men that I've met in my life.

ctx.x: Now what about, uh, Charlie Dixon? Who all did they, they were.

Charlie Dixon was one of the greatest men that I've met in my life. I wouldn't say he was the greatest musician, but he was truly a great man. And by the same token, he could play his bass and he could play his punk. He played with Singers Smith, which was another band that I didn't know, but Brad's room, Brad's first day. Charlie Dixon was a good band. Charlie Dixon was a good band. In fact, if it, uh, in fact if it wasn't for him, uh, I think Troy's family had broken up on one time for a year.
But, did he record with anybody or other than Troy?

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1973-08-06
items.q: Charlie Dixon was playing tuba and playing trombone.

ctx.x: Charlie Dixon was playing too. Charlie Dixon was playing too.
Charlie Dixon was playing tuba and playing trombone.

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1969-12-30
items.q: I can't recall who the musicians on there just by playing it, but it seems to me that I can remember that I was part of that Wabash Blues... and also Charlie Dixon.

ctx.x: And another thing he asked me about it was this Wabash Blues was supposed to be out by Troy Floyd, I guess.

Now, that's a little controversial there. Yeah. As far as I know, Troy did not make this Wabash Blues, but I have a copy of it at my home in San Antonio. I can't recall who the musicians on there just by playing it, but it seems to me that I can remember that I was part of that Wabash Blues, I'm not for sure, and also Charlie Dixon. When we recorded all these numbers, even with Hattie Brothers and the whole group, I think we recorded about three or four days. And the same musicians that were on these recordings…
Well, tell me a little bit more about Troy Floyd's band. I don't know too much about it, it's what you've told me.

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1961-05-11
items.q: Because one of them still lives here in San Antonio is the old man now, Charlie Dixon. He has all of those recordings.

ctx.x: This band that Ben Norrisingle sings these records, on these records with, were a group out of the Troy Foer's band. That is correct.
That's right. That part is right. Because one of them still lives here in San Antonio is the old man now, Charlie Dixon. He has all of those recordings.
